title: Checkout froze. Did payment succeed?
label: ASHA'S CHECKOUT
voice: Asha taps Place Order. Checkout stalls. She cannot tell whether payment succeeded. A slow request alone does not prove garbage collection caused it.
note: Customer symptom first. Diagnose the cause before changing flags.

title: The heap is Java's workbench
label: WHAT GARBAGE COLLECTION DOES
voice: The Java heap holds objects. Garbage collection reclaims unreachable objects. Some phases pause application threads; other phases run alongside them.
note: Reachable objects stay. Unreachable objects can be reclaimed.

title: 2,000 ms request. 300 ms pause.
label: FOLLOW THE TIMELINE
voice: This example request takes two seconds. An overlapping pause lasts three hundred milliseconds. The bank also takes time. Do not blame the entire delay on garbage collection.
note: Constructed evidence on one server; no benchmark claim.

title: An overlap is a clue, not a verdict
label: COMPARE THE EVIDENCE
voice: Match request traces and pause logs from the same server. Check payment waits, database spans, and CPU before deciding what to fix.
note: Intervals can overlap. Do not add the same time twice.

title: Fix proven redundant work
label: PROFILE, CHANGE, REPEAT
voice: Use Java Flight Recorder to find allocation hotspots. Remove redundant work without changing order totals. Compare the same workload before choosing another collector.
note: Fewer unnecessary objects; unchanged business calculations.

title: Responsive checkout. Correct payment.
label: VALIDATE AND RECOVER
voice: Validate tail latency, errors, memory, and CPU. Keep the original payment identity and reconcile uncertain outcomes. A timeout is not proof of failed payment.
note: Confirm only after an authoritative payment result.
